newsitem.title: EGYPT: Banks, cements send Egypt share prices higher.
newsitem.headline: Banks, cements send Egypt share prices higher.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose again on Monday after last week's doldrums, driven by gains in the blue-chip cement and banking sectors.

The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index inched 2.45 points higher to close at 348.14 points -- slightly better than last week's five-month lows. Turnover was an average 49.08 million pounds ($14.46 million).

"These price gains are mainly due to the mutual funds buying heavily to have positive results at the end of the financial year," said broker Walid el-Khouli of El-Rashad Securities Brokerage. The year ends on Monday, June 30.
"This is not an uptrend. The factors that have driven the market down have not changed but we expect it to pick up after a few public offerings hit the bourse," he added.
Last week, the all-share index plummeted to its lowest level since January and analysts said the market was in desperate need of new issues to pick up.

On Monday, the state offered investors at least 10 percent of a cotton ginning firm. Monday is also the last day for investors to buy into Alexandria Flour Mills, the latest offering in that popular sector.
The privatised flour mills continued to attract investors' attention but the banks and cement sectors generated most of the day's activity.

Misr International Bank/MIBANK, which issued global depository receipts now listed in London, was the day's busiest stock with more than six million pounds worth of turnover. The shares rose 29.49 pounds to 619.32 pounds.
Commercial International Bank (CIB) was also heavily traded and shares gained 0.85 to close at 71.1 pounds.
National Societe Generale Bank continued to draw investors for the second day running but slipped 0.25 to 80.75.
Among the cements, Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA was the busiest stock, rising 0.52 to 71.92 pounds. "Helwan is a steal at this price. This activity is understandable," Khouli said.
Some of the activity also spilled over onto Amriya Cement which edged up 0.8 pounds to 82.8 pounds.

Brokers said foreign investors were also buying share blocks in the country's monopoly cigarette manufacturer Eastern Company. The shares closed unchanged at 86 pounds after trading worth more than four million pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 474.01 points from 465.94 points on Sunday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms gained slightly to 258.23 from 257.69 points.
Of the 86 shares traded, 40 rose, 28 fell while 18 ended unchanged.
